observations.reading: The compact panel links the marked pair to four alternating half-hour periods. The revised image labels the diagonal as feasible pairs and the fixed sum as the consequence of one person’s capacity.
observations.annotation_burden: The direct A and B labels distinguish the blocks in colour and greyscale. The point, diagonal label and capacity annotations remain separate.
observations.reproduction: The historical compact prototype retains the geometry of the revised image. The audit measures its new 152.4 by 80 mm standalone PDF; the prototype retains its earlier wording.

observations.reading: The bottom timeline prototype displays the same four periods across a longer horizontal axis. The axes and task labels give the same quantities.
observations.annotation_burden: The extra horizontal space enlarges the timeline. The shorter panel in the selected design already shows every half-hour boundary and task label.
observations.reproduction: The alternative has a separate full-width timeline beneath the feasible-set panels, increasing the total figure height to 112 mm.

initial_reconstruction.claim: One person has two hours to complete one person-hour on each task. Their first-hour task totals must add to one. Four alternating half-hour blocks realise the midpoint.
quantities: Panel (a) measures first-hour person-hours on each task. The shaded square includes the pairs allowed by the separate bounds and the diagonal gives their feasible subset.
Panel (b) places the summed marginal interval from zero to two and the joint total of one on the same person-hour scale.
Panel (c) shows elapsed hours and assigns each half-hour to A or B.
initial_reconstruction.evidence_status: The example stipulates the totals. The schedule depicts one possible allocation that satisfies them.
initial_reconstruction.scope: The exact sum follows from the stipulated work exhausting one person’s available time in both hours.
unintended_inferences: A reader could interpret the shaded square as jointly feasible. The diagonal label, capacity annotations and caption distinguish the two sets.
The four-block schedule illustrates the midpoint. Other schedules can realise the same point.

matches: Both axis totals at the marked point are one half of a person-hour. Their sum matches the single diamond in panel (b).
The alternating half-hour task labels agree with the midpoint and the two whole-window totals.
Colour and greyscale show the same task labels, diagonal, interval caps and position of the diamond.

The alternative text names both first-hour task axes and the person-hour scale, explains why points on either side of the diagonal exceed the available time, and describes the four blocks that realise the midpoint.

findings.description: The revised text labels the diagonal and names the capacity assumption responsible for the fixed sum.
findings.reason: The rebuilt labels fit at the intended size in the rendered figure. The caption explains why both hours must be full and identifies panel (c) as one possible schedule.

findings.description: Finishing the requirements was not an input to the two-hour example.
findings.reason: The caption now says that the task totals use the entire shift. The independent reader recovered the feasible diagonal, fixed first-hour total and nonunique midpoint schedule from the revised caption and original image, then compared that reading with the specification.

audit_warning_dispositions.reason: The standalone class reports that shell escape is disabled. This figure uses ordinary TikZ and was rendered with shell escape disabled.

limitations: Human interpretation benefit remains unmeasured by agent screening.
The review compared the revised colour and greyscale rendering against the caption, the two existing layouts and the numerical construction. The proof of the full attainable set is in the article.
The original review covers the unchanged vector artwork and layout comparisons. An independent editorial review of the caption covers its account of the plotted quantities and schedules.
